topics.description: The two sovereign states occupying the Korean Peninsula, separated by the Korean Demilitarized Zone after the Korean War armistice.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Two answers required. The “Peace Village” is on the border between these two countries, which was created by a 1953 armistice signed in Panmunjom. The Sunshine Policy attempts to improve relations between these two countries. The 38th parallel was used to demarcate (*) the Demilitarized Zone that separates, for 10 points, what two Asian nations that share a peninsula that contains cities like Seoul and Pyongyang?

topics.description: The institution and legal status of enslaved people in ancient Greek and Roman societies.

parts.label: L
parts.question: In a play by this author, the title character is saved when Trygaeus (trug-AY-us) rides a dung beetle to  heaven. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name this author of Peace as well as a play in which Philocleon (fil-AH-KLEE-on) is addicted to  court cases, The Wasps.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] In this Aristophanes play, Dionysus and Xanthias (ZAN-thee-us) travel to the underworld to bring  back Euripides (yur-IP-id-eez). The title creatures of this play chant “Brekekekéx-koáx-koáx.”

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] Xanthias has this relationship to Dionysus at the beginning of the play, though the roles later  switch. The Roman playwright Terence was released from this status as an appreciation of his talent.

topics.description: The system of forced labor and legal bondage in Brazil that was abolished by the 1888 Golden Law.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Communities called quilombos (kee-LAHM-bohs) were occupied by people who escaped from this  institution. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this institution abolished in Brazil via the Golden Law, ending decades of forced labor.

parts.label: B
parts.question: The Golden Law was passed by Princess Isabel, the daughter of this Brazilian emperor who joined  Argentina and Uruguay in the War of the Triple Alliance.

parts.label: C
parts.question: The 1835 Malê (mah-LAY) rebellion is named after the term then used in Brazil for these people.  The Spanish explorer Estevanico (est-ay-BAN-ee-koh) and the South Carolina slave Bilalia Fula (bee- LAH-lee-ah FOO-lah) were among the first of these people in North America whose names are known.

topics.description: Iranian Shi'a cleric and revolutionary leader who led the 1979 Iranian Revolution and became the first Supreme Leader of Iran.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: An instigating factor for this event was the death of over sixty people in Jaleh (JAH-leh) Square  on “Black Friday.” This event ultimately brought to power a man who advocated the  Guardianship of the Jurist system. During this event, the SAVAK (SAH-vahk) secret police were  dissolved and a man whose ideas were popularized on clandestine (*) cassette tapes returned from  exile in Najaf (nah-JAHF). Student supporters of this event stormed an American embassy and took 66  hostages. The Pahlavi (PAH-lah-vee) Dynasty ended in, for 10 points, what 1979 event that brought  Ayatollah Khomeini (AI-uh-toh-lah koh-may-NEE) to power?
parts.answer: Iranian Revolution of 1979 [or Islamic Revolution; or Enqelāb-e Eslāmī]

parts.label: L
parts.question: For 10 points each, answer some questions about the SAVAK secret police force:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] SAVAK was active in this country until its 1979 revolution, which saw the overthrow of its Shah Mohammad Reza Pahlavi. More than 50 Americans were held hostage in this country’s city of Tehran.
parts.answer: Iran [or Islamic Republic of Iran or Jomhuri-ye Eslami-ye Iran; accept Iranian Revolution]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] After SAVAK’s dissolution, many of its members became members of SAVAMA, an intelligence agency under this ruler. This first supreme leader of Iran took power in the Iranian Revolution.
parts.answer: Ayatollah Khomeini [or Ruhollah Khomeini or Sayyid Ruhollah Musavi Khomeini; prompt on Ayatollah; reject “Khamenei”]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] A large 1978 fire in the “Rex” one of these places may have been intentionally set by the SAVAK secret police. Swedish Prime Minister Olof Palme was assassinated while walking home from one of these places.
parts.answer: cinemas [or movie theaters or the movies; accept Cinema Rex; accept Grand Cinema]

topics.description: Clinker-built Scandinavian sailing and rowing vessels used during the Viking Age for raiding, warfare, trade, exploration, transport, and burial customs.

parts.label: L
parts.question: These objects were constructed from overlapping planks of split wood fastened with iron rivets in a method known as “lapstrake” or “clinker.” For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name these objects, examples of which have been excavated from burial mounds at Oseberg and Gokstad. Variants of these objects include skeids and karves.
parts.answer: longships [or longboats; prompt on ships or boats; prompt on but DO NOT REVEAL Viking ships]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] These seafaring Scandinavian people made heavy use of longships to conduct trade and carry out raids during the Middle Ages.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] This Viking explorer probably used a knarr, a type of Norse cargo vessel similar to a longship, in his expeditions to Vinland. This explorer is believed to be the first European to travel to North America.
parts.answer: Leif Erikson [or Leif Erikson or Leiv Eiriksson or Leif the Lucky]

parts.label: L
parts.question: One of these people named Harald Hardrada lost at the Battle of Stamford Bridge. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Name these warrior seafarers that ravaged the coasts of Great Britain in the late first millennium. They hailed from Scandinavia and had kings such as Cnut (k’NOOT) and Sven Forkbeard.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] Vikings traversed the oceans in these narrow oared boats. Accomplished warriors were sometimes buried or cremated with them.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Vikings were the first to settle this modern-day country long-term. The Althing, which was founded in the year 930, is the parliament of this country, which is governed from Reykjavik.
parts.answer: Iceland [or Republic of Iceland or Lydveldid Island]

topics.description: King of England from 1272 to 1307, known for conquering Wales and campaigning against Scotland, including defeating William Wallace at Falkirk.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The Mamluks forced this ruler to retire from Crusading by having him stabbed with an allegedly poisoned  dagger. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this English king, nicknamed “Longshanks,” who won the Battle of Falkirk.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] At the Battle of Falkirk, Edward defeated this rebel leader depicted in Braveheart. This leader was not actually  sold out by Robert the Bruce prior to the Battle of Stirling Bridge.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] After winning the Battle of Falkirk, Edward was nicknamed the “Hammer of” these people. Robert the Bruce  was a king of these people, who name a country north of England.
parts.answer: Scots (or the Hammer of the Scots; or Scotland)

topics.description: Edward of Woodstock, the eldest son of Edward III and a celebrated English commander who won at Crécy and Poitiers during the Hundred Years' War.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: The costly ransom of one king in this war caused the peasants of one country to rise in the Jacquerie Rebellion. Edward the Black Prince fought in this war before dying of dysentery, and he won the battles of Poitiers (pwaht-YAY) and Crecy against King (*) John II of France in this war. For ten points, what war fought between England and France in the 14th and 15th centuries was actually 16 years longer than its name implies?

topics.description: The prehistoric and ancient historical period characterized by widespread bronze metallurgy, early civilizations, and, in many regions, the emergence of writing, preceding the Iron Age.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Marshall Sahlins argued that groups described by this term were the “original affluent society.” For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] Give this two-word term denoting early human societies that relied on killing animals and foraging for food. Groups described by this term have dwindled since the development of agriculture.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] India’s Andaman Islands are home to this tribe of uncontacted hunter-gatherers who rely on mud crab fishing. In 2018, these people killed the American missionary John Allen Chau who landed on their island.
parts.answer: North Sentinel Islanders [accept Sentinelese; accept the Sentineli]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] The Paleolithic and Neolithic periods in which hunter-gatherers thrived were succeeded by this time period, which saw the development of writing such as hieroglyphics.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Standardized bricks called talatat (TAH-lah-taht) were used to build Karnak and this city. For 10  points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name this planned Egyptian capital built by the pharaoh Akhenaten (AH-kay-NAH-ten). A  collection of diplomatic letters, mostly from Egypt's vassals in the Levant (luh-VAHNT), was found in  and named for this city.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] The Amarna letters were mostly composed in this writing system of the Ancient Near East, used for  Sumerian and Akkadian.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] The Amarna letters were written in this broad historical period. The Mediterranean-wide “collapse”  at the end of this period is linked to 12th-century BC invasions by the Sea Peoples.

topics.description: The 19th-century political and nationalist movement that unified the Italian states into the Kingdom of Italy.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: To garner international support for this cause, Count Cavour entered Piedmont-Sardinia into the Crimean War. The success of this cause resulted in the crowning of Victor-Emmanuel II as king. The Red Shirts advanced this cause under (*) Giuseppi Garibaldi by conquering the Kingdom of the Two Sicilies. For 10 points, what 19th century cause sought to consolidate provinces like the Papal States and Venice into a single country?

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This cause defeated the black nobility that supported the independence of Pius IX. A supporter of this cause wrote an open letter to Charles Albert and was a member of the Carbonari. In the Plombières Agreement, Napoleon III agreed to support this cause at the behest of Count Cavour. At the battle of Calatafimi, supporters of this cause called Redshirts defeated the Kingdom of the Two (*) Sicilies. This cause was accomplished when Victor Emmanuel II ascended the throne of a new country with the support of Giuseppe Garibaldi. For 10 points, name this nationalist cause to create a new kingdom led from Rome.
parts.answer: Italian Unification [accept word forms such as the unification of Italy; or the Risorgimento]

topics.description: The 1917 German diplomatic message proposing an alliance with Mexico against the United States, whose interception contributed to U.S. entry into World War I.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Part of the U.S. Army 85th Division was diverted from this war to join the Polar Bear  Expedition. A predominantly Black regiment in this war was nicknamed the Harlem Hellfighters.  This war marked the peak in popularity of the term (*) “doughboys” for front-line soldiers. The  American Expeditionary Forces were led by John Pershing in this war, which the U.S. joined after a  telegram sent to Mexico from Arthur Zimmerman was intercepted. For 10 points, Woodrow Wilson led  the U.S. through what 1910s conflict?
parts.answer: World War I [or First World War; or the Great War]

parts.label: L
parts.question: Venustiano Carranza rejected an offer laid out in this document. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this document, proposing a secret alliance between Germany and Mexico. This document was intercepted and decoded by Nigel de Grey and William Reginald Hall in Room 40.
parts.answer: ANSWER: Zimmermann Telegram [or Zimmermann Note or Zimmermann Cable]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] Two years prior, German U-boats sank the Lusitania, which caused this Secretary of State to resign. This former populist presidential candidate claimed “you shall not crucify mankind” upon the title object in one speech.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] This president, despite his slogan “he kept us out of war,” entered World War I in 1917. This president gave the Fourteen Points speech.
